key_safety: Most common adverse reactions were diarrhea and rash (each 42%); ILD/pneumonitis occurred in 2.7% of patients and caused 4 treatment-related deaths; QTc prolongation (max mean change from baseline 16.2 ms) and embryo-fetal toxicity were identified as additional warnings.
target_moa: Irreversible inhibitor of EGFR harboring sensitizing mutations (exon 19 deletions, L858R) and the resistance mutation T790M, with limited activity against wild-type EGFR

_meta.indication:
TAGRISSO is indicated for the treatment of patients with metastatic epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) T790M mutation-positive non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), as detected by an FDA-approved test, who have progressed on or after EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) therapy. 
This indication is approved under accelerated approval based on tumor response rate and duration of response. Continued approval for this indication may be contingent upon verification and description of clinical benefit in confirmatory trials.

indication_details.population_restrictions: EGFR T790M mutation-positive, as detected by an FDA-approved test
indication_details.prior_therapy_required: progressed on or after EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) therapy

supplements.description: Converted osimertinib (Tagrisso) from accelerated to regular approval for "patients with metastatic EGFR T790M mutation-positive non-small cell lung cancer...whose disease has progressed on or after EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor therapy," removing the accelerated approval contingency language based on confirmatory trial AURA 3.

Expanded the indication for Tagrisso (osimertinib) to include **first-line treatment** of patients with "metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) whose tumors have epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) exon 19 deletions or exon 21 (L858R) substitution mutations, as detected by an FDA approved test," based on progression-free survival data from the FLAURA study versus erlotinib or gefitinib.

Updated the CLINICAL STUDIES section of the Tagrisso (osimertinib) label to include mature overall survival data from Study FLAURA for "previously untreated EGFR mutation-positive metastatic non-small cell lung cancer," fulfilling a postmarketing commitment; no new indication, population, or dose was added.

Approved a new indication for TAGRISSO (osimertinib) as **adjuvant therapy after tumor resection in adult patients with NSCLC** "whose tumors have epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) exon 19 deletions or exon 21 L858R mutations, as detected by an FDA-approved test."

Updated labeling only — specifically the CLINICAL STUDIES section of the Tagrisso (osimertinib) Prescribing Information to incorporate final overall survival results from the ADAURA study, fulfilling postmarketing commitment 3992-1; no new indication, population, dose, or use was approved.

Expanded indication to include Tagrisso (osimertinib) **in combination with pemetrexed and platinum-based chemotherapy** for the first-line treatment of "adult patients with locally advanced or metastatic non-small cell lung cancer whose tumors have EGFR exon 19 deletions or exon 21 L858R mutations," based on results from the FLAURA2 trial.

Expanded indication to include "adult patients with locally advanced, unresectable (stage III) non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) whose disease has not progressed during or following concurrent or sequential platinum-based chemoradiation therapy" and whose tumors harbor EGFR exon 19 deletions or exon 21 L858R mutations, as detected by an FDA-approved test.

companion_dx_detail: An FDA-approved test is required to detect EGFR exon 19 deletions or exon 21 L858R mutations (for first-line metastatic NSCLC) or EGFR T790M mutation (for previously treated metastatic NSCLC) in tumor or plasma specimens. The label directs prescribers to http://www.fda.gov/companiondiagnostics for information on FDA-approved tests for EGFR mutation detection, but does not name a specific companion diagnostic test by proprietary name.
